assessments.reasoning: Section 6.1.4 defines the String as a sequence of 16-bit unsigned elements, defines length by the number of elements, and assigns UTF-16 code-unit interpretation where text is interpreted. The same clause expressly handles unpaired surrogates.

challenge.method: Compare the specification’s element-count definition with its surrogate rules, then test a supplementary character, a lone surrogate and a base character plus combining mark.
challenge.results: The element metric counts the constituent code units. Code-point iteration over a valid surrogate pair gives a different count, and the type still admits a lone surrogate. The local Node.js v24.4.1 diagnostic agreed. Supplementary character measured 2 elements and 1 code point; lone surrogate measured 1.

limitations: The result concerns the specified String length and does not count display glyphs or user-perceived graphemes.
